title: Package Management
subtitle: apt, brew, snap — installing, updating, and removing software
author: KERNAL Team

content.code:
# Update package lists (do this before installing)
sudo apt update

# Upgrade installed packages
sudo apt upgrade
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y   # update + upgrade in one

# Install a package
sudo apt install nginx
sudo apt install git curl wget vim       # multiple packages
sudo apt install -y nginx               # -y: no confirmation prompt

# Remove a package
sudo apt remove nginx          # remove but keep config files
sudo apt purge nginx           # remove + delete config files
sudo apt autoremove            # remove unused dependencies

# Search for packages
apt search "text editor"
apt show vim                   # package details

# List installed packages
apt list --installed
dpkg -l | grep nginx           # check if nginx is installed

# Install Homebrew
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

# Install a package
brew install node
brew install git postgresql wget

# Install a GUI app (cask)
brew install --cask visual-studio-code
brew install --cask docker

# Update and upgrade
brew update              # update brew formula list
brew upgrade             # upgrade all packages
brew upgrade node        # upgrade specific package

# Remove
brew uninstall node
brew cleanup             # remove old versions

# Search
brew search redis
brew info postgresql     # package details

content.text: Always run sudo apt update before sudo apt install — without it, apt uses a stale package list and may install outdated versions or fail to find new packages.

questions.question: You want to install nginx on Ubuntu and ensure it starts automatically. Which sequence?
options: sudo apt update → sudo apt install nginx → sudo systemctl enable nginx
sudo apt install nginx (it starts automatically)
questions.explanation: sudo apt update refreshes the package list, sudo apt install nginx installs it, and sudo systemctl enable nginx configures it to start on boot. apt install starts the service immediately on Ubuntu but doesn't enable it for future reboots — enable does that. sudo systemctl start nginx starts it right now.

faq.q: Which package manager should I use on macOS?
faq.a: Homebrew (brew) is the standard. It installs into /opt/homebrew (Apple Silicon) or /usr/local (Intel) and does not require sudo for most operations. Install it first, then use brew install for command-line tools and brew install --cask for GUI apps.

examples: Dockerfiles almost always use apt-get update && apt-get install -y package to install dependencies in containers
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y is the first command every developer runs after provisioning a new server
